coincident/04-arc-vs-cubic-circle.difference: Correct now, but slow: ~9.4s per operation, all of it in intersection finding. The arc and the cubic approximating it stay within a whisker of each other along a whole quadrant, so their boxes overlap everywhere and the subdivision explores an enormous number of leaf pairs to return 3 points per pair. Needs the finder to recognize that two curves run together within tolerance over a stretch, rather than bisecting its way along it.

coincident/11-circle-vs-overlong-radii.difference: Over the 5s budget. A and B are the same unit circle, but B's radii are half what its chords need and only the centre parametrization applies the SVG F.6.6 correction — the tuple keeps `rx = 0.5`. Reconstructing a split arc through that parametrization moves it by 5e-7, which is above the `eps.point` of 4.3e-8 that `epsilonsForExtent` gives a scene this size. So the overlap detection in `groupCandidates` and the coincident-edge merge in `findVertices` both correctly judge the two representations as distinct, and the subdivision goes on bisecting along them. Fixing this means making the split of an arc reproduce its own geometry to better than `eps.point`, which is a separate problem from detecting coincidence.

conditioning/03-edge-shared-full-small-a.difference: Throws `No outer face of a component found` under the `small-and-far` conditioning — a scene 2e-3 across sitting at an offset of 1e6, where neighbouring doubles are ~2e-10 apart. Each conditioning on its own passes (`-small` and `-far` are both green), so it is the combination that loses the precision. `config.ts` is explicit that a large offset is a known separate problem that widening tolerances would conceal rather than cure, so this documents the limit rather than proposing to move it. In the production bundle it throws a raw TypeError from `WeakSet.add` in `flagFaces`.

conditioning/04-arc-shared-full-tiny.exclusion: Wrong by 0.34% to 0.82% of compared pixels at the `tiny` conditioning, where the scene is 2e-6 across — the size of the *unscaled* `EPS.point`. The shared rim itself is now handled: the arrangement comes out with the right faces (Division 1, Fracture 2) and the algebraic identities all hold. What is left is placement, `epsilonsForExtent` only ever scaling the tolerances down from a 50-unit reference, so at this extent they sit near 4e-14 and the split points land further apart than that.

touching/08-arc-shared-partial.difference: Correct now — Fracture returns the disc and the wedge as the two faces they are, where it used to merge them into one — but still over the 5s budget, at 6.9s to 16.2s per operation. The short-circuit that made `touching/09` immediate does not fire here: it recognizes a leaf pair as the same piece of curve, and only segments covering the *same* extent subdivide into leaves that match. A quarter arc against the 60 degrees of it that B shares never halves into equal pieces, so the coincident run is still bisected the whole way down. Recognizing an overlap before the leaves line up is the remaining half of this.
